title: Common Phrasal Verbs list 3
intro: Learn the most common phrasal verbs in English with the following list.

meanings: To physically see something in front of you.
To anticipate future situations.
items.example: It's time to look ahead and make plans.

items.es: menospreciar, mirar por encima del hombro
meanings: To physically see something from a high place.
When you consider someone or something inferior.
items.example: He looks down on people without money.

items.es: tener ganas de, esperar con ilusión
meanings: When you get excited about an upcoming event.
items.example: I'm looking forward to the holidays.

meanings: To pay attention to your surroundings because a potential danger.
items.example: Look out! There's a car coming.

meanings: To examine or inspect something either briefly or thoroughly.
items.example: Can you look over my essay?

meanings: When you have respect for someone else.
items.example: Kids often look up to their older siblings.

meanings: To view or gaze at something.
To consider something in a particular way.
items.example: Many people look upon him as a hero.

meanings: To flee.
items.example: The thieves made off with the money.

items.en: To make out something / to make something out
meanings: To comprehend something.
To see something when it was impossible to notice.
items.example: I can't make out what he's saying.

meanings: To compensate.
items.example: I'll make up for being late.

items.en: To make up something / to make something up
meanings: To invent something false.
To reconcile with someone.
items.example: He made up an excuse.

meanings: To faint.
To distribute something to people.
items.example: It was so hot that she passed out.

meanings: To return money you owe to someone.
To take revenge on someone.
items.example: I'll pay you back next week.

meanings: To select someone from a group of people.
To recognize or identify someone or something.
items.example: She picked out a dress for the party.

meanings: To raise something from the floor.
To learn something new.
To give someone a ride.
To collect something from somewhere.
items.example: Can you pick me up at the station?

meanings: To highlight or indicate something for someone else to see it.
items.example: She pointed out a mistake in my report.

items.es: detenerse a un lado (con un vehículo)
meanings: To move a vehicle to the side of the road.
items.example: The police told the driver to pull over.

meanings: To hang something.
To increase the prices.
items.example: We put up the decorations for the party.

meanings: To endure an unpleasant situation.
items.example: I can't put up with this noise anymore.

meanings: When you suddenly meet someone
items.example: I ran into an old friend at the supermarket.
